/-!
# Conjecture 7.27

by V. M. Levchuk

Is it true that the group $SL_n(q)$ contains, for sufficiently large $q$, a diagonal matrix
which is not contained in any proper irreducible subgroup of $SL_n(q)$ with the exception of
block-monomial ones? For $n = 2, 3$ the answer is known to be affirmative (V. M. Levchuk,
*in: Some problems of the theory of groups and rings*, Inst. of Physics SO AN SSSR,
Krasnoyarsk, 1973 (Russian)).

Here a subgroup $H \le SL_n(q)$ is *irreducible* if its natural action on $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ has
no $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspaces invariant under $H$ other than $0$ and $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, and $H$ is
*block-monomial* (imprimitive) if it preserves some decomposition
$\mathbb{F}_q^n = V_1 \oplus \dots \oplus V_k$ into $k \ge 2$ subspaces of equal dimension,
every element of $H$ permuting the summands $V_i$; in a basis adapted to the decomposition the
elements of $H$ are block-monomial matrices. Some such exception is necessary: every diagonal
matrix lies in the subgroup of monomial matrices, which is block-monomial (with $k = n$) and
irreducible for large $q$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.toLin'` (used as the building block), `Representation.ofMulAction` (permutation representations only), `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.toLin`.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.27».naturalRep
justification.why_needed: To apply Mathlib's `Representation.IsIrreducible` to a subgroup H ≤ SL(n,F), the natural action of H on `Fin n → F` must be packaged as a `Representation F H (Fin n → F)`; Mathlib has no such representation for matrix groups. blocks.name: naturalRep
blocks.text:
/-- The natural representation of a subgroup $H \le SL_n(F)$ on $F^n$, given by
matrix-vector multiplication. -/
def naturalRep (H : Subgroup SL(n, F)) : Representation F H (Fin n → F) :=
  LinearEquiv.automorphismGroup.toLinearMapMonoidHom.comp
    (SpecialLinearGroup.toLin'.comp H.subtype)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem naturalRep_apply (H : Subgroup SL(n, F)) (h : H) (v : Fin n → F) :
    naturalRep H h v = (h : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) F) *ᵥ v := by
  simp [naturalRep, SpecialLinearGroup.toLin'_apply]

def IsBlockMonomial (H : Subgroup SL(n, F)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (V : Fin k → Submodule F (Fin n → F)), 2 ≤ k ∧ DirectSum.IsInternal V ∧
    (∀ i j, Module.finrank F (V i) = Module.finrank F (V j)) ∧
    ∀ h ∈ H, ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k),
      ∀ i, (V i).map (SpecialLinearGroup.toLin' h).toLinearMap = V (σ i)
blocks.docstring:
A subgroup $H \le SL_n(F)$ is *block-monomial* if there is a decomposition
$F^n = V_1 \oplus \dots \oplus V_k$ into $k \ge 2$ subspaces of equal dimension such that
every element of $H$ permutes the summands $V_1, \dots, V_k$. In a basis adapted to the
decomposition, the elements of $H$ are then block-monomial matrices: each block row and each

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.diagonalSubgroup` / `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.diagonalSubgroup` in FormalConjecturesForMathlib (diagonal, not block-monomial), `DirectSum.IsInternal`, `Submodule.map` (used as building blocks).
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.27».IsBlockMonomial
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has a notion of block-monomial / imprimitive linear group (Aschbacher class C₂): a subgroup preserving a decomposition Fⁿ = V₁ ⊕ … ⊕ V_k (k ≥ 2, equal dimensions) and permuting the summands. Defined with `DirectSum.IsInternal`, `Module.finrank`, and `Equiv.Perm`. API lemma `IsBlockMonomial.mono` (closed under passing to subgroups) and test lemma `isBlockMonomial_bot` (coordinate-line decomposition, the monomial case k = n) are proved.

blocks.name: IsBlockMonomial
blocks.text:
/-- A subgroup $H \le SL_n(F)$ is *block-monomial* if there is a decomposition
$F^n = V_1 \oplus \dots \oplus V_k$ into $k \ge 2$ subspaces of equal dimension such that
every element of $H$ permutes the summands $V_1, \dots, V_k$. In a basis adapted to the
decomposition, the elements of $H$ are then block-monomial matrices: each block row and each
block column contains exactly one non-zero block. -/
def IsBlockMonomial (H : Subgroup SL(n, F)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (V : Fin k → Submodule F (Fin n → F)), 2 ≤ k ∧ DirectSum.IsInternal V ∧
    (∀ i j, Module.finrank F (V i) = Module.finrank F (V j)) ∧
    ∀ h ∈ H, ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k),
      ∀ i, (V i).map (SpecialLinearGroup.toLin' h).toLinearMap = V (σ i)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBlockMonomial.mono {H K : Subgroup SL(n, F)} (hHK : H ≤ K) (hK : IsBlockMonomial K) :
    IsBlockMonomial H := by
  obtain ⟨k, V, hk, hV, hdim, hperm⟩ := hK
  exact ⟨k, V, hk, hV, hdim, fun h hh => hperm h (hHK hh)⟩

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isBlockMonomial_bot (hn : 2 ≤ n) : IsBlockMonomial (⊥ : Subgroup SL(n, F)) := by
  refine ⟨n, fun i => Submodule.span F {Pi.basisFun F (Fin n) i}, hn, ?_, fun i j => ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [DirectSum.isInternal_submodule_iff_iSupIndep_and_iSup_eq_top]
    exact ⟨(Pi.basisFun F (Fin n)).linearIndependent.iSupIndep_span_singleton,
      by rw [← Submodule.span_range_eq_iSup, (Pi.basisFun F (Fin n)).span_eq]⟩
  · rw [finrank_span_singleton ((Pi.basisFun F (Fin n)).ne_zero i),
      finrank_span_singleton ((Pi.basisFun F (Fin n)).ne_zero j)]
  · intro h hh
    rw [Subgroup.mem_bot] at hh
    subst hh
    exact ⟨1, fun i => by simp⟩
blocks.docstring:
The trivial subgroup is block-monomial for the decomposition of $F^n$ into the $n$
coordinate lines (the case $k = n$ of "monomial" matrices).
blocks.name: isBlockMonomial_bot
blocks.text:
/-- The trivial subgroup is block-monomial for the decomposition of $F^n$ into the $n$
coordinate lines (the case $k = n$ of "monomial" matrices). -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isBlockMonomial_bot (hn : 2 ≤ n) : IsBlockMonomial (⊥ : Subgroup SL(n, F)) := by
  refine ⟨n, fun i => Submodule.span F {Pi.basisFun F (Fin n) i}, hn, ?_, fun i j => ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [DirectSum.isInternal_submodule_iff_iSupIndep_and_iSup_eq_top]
    exact ⟨(Pi.basisFun F (Fin n)).linearIndependent.iSupIndep_span_singleton,
      by rw [← Submodule.span_range_eq_iSup, (Pi.basisFun F (Fin n)).span_eq]⟩
  · rw [finrank_span_singleton ((Pi.basisFun F (Fin n)).ne_zero i),
      finrank_span_singleton ((Pi.basisFun F (Fin n)).ne_zero j)]
  · intro h hh
    rw [Subgroup.mem_bot] at hh
    subst hh
    exact ⟨1, fun i => by simp⟩

proper irreducible subgroup of $SL_n(F)$ containing $d$ is block-monomial.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None; it is a problem-specific abbreviation composed of `Matrix.IsDiag`, `Representation.IsIrreducible`, and `IsBlockMonomial`.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.27».HasLevchukDiagonal
justification.why_needed: Names the core property shared by both slots (SL_n(F) contains a diagonal matrix lying in no proper irreducible subgroup except block-monomial ones), so the two theorems cannot diverge and each reads as `∀ n …, ∃ q₀, ∀ F, q₀ ≤ |F| → HasLevchukDiagonal n F`.

blocks.name: HasLevchukDiagonal
blocks.text:
/-- `HasLevchukDiagonal n F` says that $SL_n(F)$ contains a diagonal matrix $d$ such that every
proper irreducible subgroup of $SL_n(F)$ containing $d$ is block-monomial. -/
def HasLevchukDiagonal (n : ℕ) (F : Type*) [Field F] : Prop :=
  ∃ d : SL(n, F), (d : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) F).IsDiag ∧
    ∀ H : Subgroup SL(n, F), H ≠ ⊤ → (naturalRep H).IsIrreducible → d ∈ H → IsBlockMonomial H

which is not contained in any proper irreducible subgroup of $SL_n(q)$ with the exception of

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question, so `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n ≥ 2, ∃ q₀, ∀ prime powers q ≥ q₀, ∃ diagonal d ∈ SL_n(F_q), ∀ proper subgroup H < SL_n(F_q) acting irreducibly on F_q^n, d ∈ H → H is block-monomial`; the threshold q₀ implicitly depends on n, 'irreducible' refers to the natural action on F_q^n, and 'block-monomial' means H stabilises a decomposition F_q^n = V_1 ⊕ … ⊕ V_k (k ≥ 2, equal dimensions) permuting the summands (the exception is needed since every diagonal matrix lies in the monomial subgroup); n = 1 is degenerate and should be excluded.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematics and match the decomposition table (∀ n ≥ 2, ∃ q₀ depending on n, ∀ finite fields with |F| ≥ q₀, ∃ diagonal d ∈ SL(n,F), every proper subgroup H ∋ d acting irreducibly on Fⁿ over F stabilises some decomposition into k ≥ 2 equal-dimension summands, permuting them). c08 chosen for style/robustness: it reuses Mathlib's `Representation.IsIrreducible` (I verified in a scratch file that it forces nontriviality and that every H-invariant subspace is ⊥ or ⊤), uses an explicit permutation σ in the block-monomial definition, factors the per-field property into a documented def, and supplies proved API/test lemmas for the bespoke definition as CONTRIBUTING requests. Only edit: expanded the module docstring to record the interpretation (irreducible over F_q; block-monomial = imprimitive, up to conjugacy).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.27

by V. M. Levchuk

Is it true that the group $SL_n(q)$ contains, for sufficiently large $q$, a diagonal matrix
which is not contained in any proper irreducible subgroup of $SL_n(q)$ with the exception of
block-monomial ones? For $n = 2, 3$ the answer is known to be affirmative (V. M. Levchuk,
*in: Some problems of the theory of groups and rings*, Inst. of Physics SO AN SSSR,
Krasnoyarsk, 1973 (Russian)).

Here a subgroup $H \le SL_n(q)$ is *irreducible* if its natural action on $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ has
no $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspaces invariant under $H$ other than $0$ and $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, and $H$ is
*block-monomial* (imprimitive) if it preserves some decomposition
$\mathbb{F}_q^n = V_1 \oplus \dots \oplus V_k$ into $k \ge 2$ subspaces of equal dimension,
every element of $H$ permuting the summands $V_i$; in a basis adapted to the decomposition the
elements of $H$ are block-monomial matrices. Some such exception is necessary: every diagonal
matrix lies in the subgroup of monomial matrices, which is block-monomial (with $k = n$) and
irreducible for large $q$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open Matrix
open scoped MatrixGroups

namespace Kourovka.«7.27»

variable {n : ℕ} {F : Type*} [Field F]

/-- The natural representation of a subgroup $H \le SL_n(F)$ on $F^n$, given by
matrix-vector multiplication. -/
def naturalRep (H : Subgroup SL(n, F)) : Representation F H (Fin n → F) :=
  LinearEquiv.automorphismGroup.toLinearMapMonoidHom.comp
    (SpecialLinearGroup.toLin'.comp H.subtype)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem naturalRep_apply (H : Subgroup SL(n, F)) (h : H) (v : Fin n → F) :
    naturalRep H h v = (h : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) F) *ᵥ v := by
  simp [naturalRep, SpecialLinearGroup.toLin'_apply]

/-- A subgroup $H \le SL_n(F)$ is *block-monomial* if there is a decomposition
$F^n = V_1 \oplus \dots \oplus V_k$ into $k \ge 2$ subspaces of equal dimension such that
every element of $H$ permutes the summands $V_1, \dots, V_k$. In a basis adapted to the
decomposition, the elements of $H$ are then block-monomial matrices: each block row and each
block column contains exactly one non-zero block. -/
def IsBlockMonomial (H : Subgroup SL(n, F)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (V : Fin k → Submodule F (Fin n → F)), 2 ≤ k ∧ DirectSum.IsInternal V ∧
    (∀ i j, Module.finrank F (V i) = Module.finrank F (V j)) ∧
    ∀ h ∈ H, ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k),
      ∀ i, (V i).map (SpecialLinearGroup.toLin' h).toLinearMap = V (σ i)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBlockMonomial.mono {H K : Subgroup SL(n, F)} (hHK : H ≤ K) (hK : IsBlockMonomial K) :
    IsBlockMonomial H := by
  obtain ⟨k, V, hk, hV, hdim, hperm⟩ := hK
  exact ⟨k, V, hk, hV, hdim, fun h hh => hperm h (hHK hh)⟩

/-- The trivial subgroup is block-monomial for the decomposition of $F^n$ into the $n$
coordinate lines (the case $k = n$ of "monomial" matrices). -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isBlockMonomial_bot (hn : 2 ≤ n) : IsBlockMonomial (⊥ : Subgroup SL(n, F)) := by
  refine ⟨n, fun i => Submodule.span F {Pi.basisFun F (Fin n) i}, hn, ?_, fun i j => ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [DirectSum.isInternal_submodule_iff_iSupIndep_and_iSup_eq_top]
    exact ⟨(Pi.basisFun F (Fin n)).linearIndependent.iSupIndep_span_singleton,
      by rw [← Submodule.span_range_eq_iSup, (Pi.basisFun F (Fin n)).span_eq]⟩
  · rw [finrank_span_singleton ((Pi.basisFun F (Fin n)).ne_zero i),
      finrank_span_singleton ((Pi.basisFun F (Fin n)).ne_zero j)]
  · intro h hh
    rw [Subgroup.mem_bot] at hh
    subst hh
    exact ⟨1, fun i => by simp⟩

/-- `HasLevchukDiagonal n F` says that $SL_n(F)$ contains a diagonal matrix $d$ such that every
proper irreducible subgroup of $SL_n(F)$ containing $d$ is block-monomial. -/
def HasLevchukDiagonal (n : ℕ) (F : Type*) [Field F] : Prop :=
  ∃ d : SL(n, F), (d : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) F).IsDiag ∧
    ∀ H : Subgroup SL(n, F), H ≠ ⊤ → (naturalRep H).IsIrreducible → d ∈ H → IsBlockMonomial H

/--
Is it true that the group $SL_n(q)$ contains, for sufficiently large $q$, a diagonal matrix
which is not contained in any proper irreducible subgroup of $SL_n(q)$ with the exception of
block-monomial ones?

That is: for every $n \ge 2$ is there a bound $q_0$ such that for every finite field
$\mathbb{F}_q$ with $q \ge q_0$ there is a diagonal $d \in SL_n(q)$ such that every proper
irreducible subgroup of $SL_n(q)$ containing $d$ is block-monomial? The bound $q_0$ may depend
on $n$. The case $n = 1$ is excluded since $SL_1(q)$ is trivial.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.27» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∃ q₀ : ℕ, ∀ (F : Type) [Field F] [Fintype F],
      q₀ ≤ Fintype.card F → HasLevchukDiagonal n F := by
  sorry

/--
For $n = 2, 3$ the answer to Problem 7.27 is affirmative (V. M. Levchuk, 1973): for
$n \in \{2, 3\}$ and all sufficiently large $q$, the group $SL_n(q)$ contains a diagonal matrix
which is not contained in any proper irreducible subgroup of $SL_n(q)$ with the exception of
block-monomial ones.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.27».variants.n_two_three :
    ∀ n ∈ ({2, 3} : Set ℕ), ∃ q₀ : ℕ, ∀ (F : Type) [Field F] [Fintype F],
      q₀ ≤ Fintype.card F → HasLevchukDiagonal n F := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.27»

items: "Sufficiently large q" is formalized as `∃ q₀ : ℕ, ∀ (F : Type) [Field F] [Fintype F], q₀ ≤ Fintype.card F → …`, with q₀ chosen after n (so it may depend on n). Quantifying over finite fields of cardinality ≥ q₀ is equivalent to quantifying over prime powers q ≥ q₀ since finite fields are determined up to isomorphism by their cardinality and the property is isomorphism-invariant.

"Irreducible" means irreducible over F_q for the natural action on F_q^n (not absolutely irreducible), formalized with Mathlib's `Representation.IsIrreducible` (= `IsSimpleOrder` of subrepresentations), which also requires F_q^n ≠ 0; this is automatic for n ≥ 2.

"Block-monomial" is read conjugacy-invariantly: H stabilizes some decomposition F^n = V₁ ⊕ … ⊕ V_k into k ≥ 2 subspaces of equal dimension, each element of H permuting the summands (Aschbacher class C₂ / imprimitive). The decomposition is not required to consist of coordinate subspaces of the standard basis. Equal dimension is included per the standard definition; it is automatic for irreducible H.

"With the exception of block-monomial ones" is read as: every proper irreducible subgroup containing d is a *subgroup of* some block-monomial group. The stricter reading (only the full block-monomial groups themselves are excepted) would be false already for n = 3 (e.g. ⟨d, 3-cycle permutation matrix⟩ is irreducible and proper in the monomial group), contradicting Levchuk's affirmative answer, so it cannot be the intended meaning.

k = 1 is excluded from block-monomial (`2 ≤ k`), otherwise every subgroup would be block-monomial and the statement trivially true. `H ≠ ⊤` encodes "proper"; without it the statement is trivially false.
n = 1 is excluded (`2 ≤ n`) as degenerate (SL₁(q) is trivial; the statement would be vacuously true there). n = 2 is the smallest case and is non-degenerate.
"Diagonal matrix" means diagonal with respect to the standard basis, i.e. `Matrix.IsDiag` of the underlying matrix of an element of `SL(n, F)`.
The solved variant is stated for `∀ n ∈ ({2, 3} : Set ℕ)` in a single theorem, as allowed by the decomposition notes, rather than as two separate theorems.

Interpretation choices (shared by all candidates and prescribed by the table): (1) 'sufficiently large q' = ∃ q₀ with q₀ chosen after n; prime powers q are encoded by quantifying over all finite fields F : Type with q = Fintype.card F, equivalent since finite fields are determined by cardinality and every prime power occurs. (2) 'irreducible' = irreducible over F_q for the natural action on F_q^n (not absolutely irreducible). (3) 'block-monomial' is read conjugacy-invariantly (imprimitive: H permutes the summands of SOME direct-sum decomposition of F_q^n into k ≥ 2 subspaces of equal dimension). A stricter reading — blocks must be coordinate subspaces of the standard basis — is also defensible since d is diagonal in the standard basis; the two readings coincide for a diagonal d whose n!-th power still has distinct eigenvalues (the natural witness), but they differ as formal statements. The table prescribes the basis-free reading and it is the standard notion of imprimitive linear group, so it was kept; this is the main residual ambiguity. (4) 'with the exception of block-monomial ones' is read as: every proper irreducible H containing d is block-monomial (contained in a block-monomial group); the alternative 'only the full block-monomial groups are excepted' would be false already for n = 3, contradicting Levchuk's affirmative answer. (5) n = 1 excluded (SL_1 trivial); 'diagonal' = Matrix.IsDiag of the underlying matrix; 'proper' = H ≠ ⊤. The 'Similar problems ... other Chevalley groups' sentence was not formalized per the instructions.
statement: Is it true that the group $SL_n(q)$ contains, for sufficiently large $q$, a diagonal matrix which is not contained in any proper irreducible subgroup of $SL_n(q)$ with the exception of block-monomial ones? For $n=2,\, 3$ the answer is known to be affirmative (V. M. Levchuk, in: Some problems of the theory of groups and rings, Inst. of Physics SO AN SSSR, Krasnoyarsk, 1973 (Russian)). Similar problems are interesting for other Chevalley groups.
